Every text below is copied word for word from one of the four CVs in _sources, each of which passed a fact-trace / recruiter / skeptic review; the only changes allowed are stripping HTML tags, decoding entities, turning a leading bold lead-in into **Lead.** (the renderer prints it bold) and dropping link markup (the visible words stay). Where two CVs carry the same fact only one wording is kept (the most recent, unless an older one stands alone better), and a line that points elsewhere ("above", "described"), addresses a reader, names an employer applied to or speaks to one job is left out. To add a line: first get it into a CV that passes the same review, add that CV to _sources, then copy the line here verbatim with its src and re-run the verbatim check (every text must be found in its src CV).

summary.text: Since 2025 I have owned the AI products of AIdeazz AI Lab end to end: I decide what gets built and in what order, write the requirements, decide the tests a change must pass, launch it, and measure the result in production. Specialized AI agents do much of the implementation; the product decisions, the acceptance and the outcome are mine.

In 2024–2025 I was Operational Co-Founder of OmniBazaar, a decentralized e-commerce marketplace, where I led strategic planning and its operating structure. From 2011 to 2018 I was Deputy CEO for Corporate Governance and Chief Legal Officer of a ~60-person company that moved public services into electronic form: I ran the board process for stakeholders drawn mainly from the regional government, carried its decisions through to implementation, and managed those electronic-service projects from the legal side.

I find the work that should not be done by hand, decide what to automate and where a human must stay in control, then own the automation from discovery through deployment and monitoring. Since 2025 I have run AIdeazz AI Lab, where 15 production services and 20 scheduled jobs carry out operations, CRM and outreach, research and publishing work every day.

I operate an AI-native development environment where specialized agents handle much of the implementation execution. I own requirements, architecture, orchestration, evaluation, deployment, monitoring and production decisions. Claude and ChatGPT are daily tools; priorities, verification and consequential decisions stay with me.

bullets.text: **AI Visibility Audit API — idea to launch to measured use.** A public product, launched July 2026: anyone pastes a website address and, with no login, gets a score for how well ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude can find and cite it. I designed the rubric, 34 checks in 4 weighted categories, and an output a non-technical buyer can act on: a grade, and the fix and the reason for every failed check. 420+ audits across 210+ sites, most of them run by my own outreach agents before a new prospect is contacted; in the logs, 48 audits of 16 different sites came from 16 addresses that are not my laptop or our server.
My acceptance criteria are tests: a change is accepted only when the tests and the production logs prove it works. 600+ automated tests across unit, integration and evaluation layers.

The spec says what the model decides and what code decides: hard facts in a posting, such as a country restriction or a pay figure, are checked in code; judgment calls go to the model. When one of my override rules wrongly let three postings through because it saw "LATAM" and ignored "U.S. only", I changed it to ask the same location checker the filters use.

**Prioritized from outcome data.** In my job-search pipeline, outcome labels showed one role category made up 7 of the 12 postings I rejected but only 2 of the 12 I rated positive. I cut it from targeting within a day and re-pointed the searches to the categories that fit.

**Said no on evidence.** Two job boards looked equally good on their websites, but one had no posting newer than 33 days and 91% past their own expiry. I rejected it, connected the other, and wrote down why.
**Decided under uncertainty.** When a vendor retired the AI models my services used, I moved all six products onto a five-provider fallback chain that week, with no outage.

Trial sign-ups to EspaLuz, my language-tutor bot, had never reached the CRM since launch, while the sender's log looked healthy. I found it by auditing from the receiving end, fixed it and backfilled all 28 lost users.

Built a reply detector so a prospect's answer is not lost in the inbox: it reads two inboxes and matches every sender against the CRM. Replayed on 60 days of real mail, it narrowed 2,432 emails to the 73 from people linked to a deal, including a prospect's reply that had sat unseen for nearly eight weeks. Live, it checks every 10 minutes and alerts me with the deal linked.

An upgrade to my AI screening step (retrieval, RAG) scored lower on a test set built from my own past decisions, so it stayed switched off: a change that measures worse does not ship, however sophisticated.
A new job source cleared my live filter 72% of the time, across all 345 of its postings, so it stayed.

I fix the measurement itself: my screening replay was grading against blank postings, so its score measured the blank. Each decision is now stored with its real posting and replayed before a change ships.
"It ran" is not "it worked": one search path ran on schedule with its filters silently switched off. The first fixed run rejected five junk results that used to become CRM deals.
Found a spending cap that could never fire: the budget guard read a price field the vendor never sends. Fixed it against the vendor's real response and published the postmortem.

Set the coordination protocol three AI coding agents follow even though they cannot see each other's chats: claim before touching shared systems, a handoff block on every pause (done / next / verified by / risk), and every work product in a file or the CRM, never only in a chat.

Every CRM stage is named for whose move it is; one approved send moves the deal, stamps delivery and books the follow-up. A daily read-back audit checks every priority deal against a six-part completeness standard and alerts on any gap.
A morning briefing replaced opening records one by one: the day's priority queue, each item with a sourced company summary where sources exist.
I publish failures openly: 20+ named postmortems in a public AI Operations Wiki, plus an AI Operations SOP.

steps.title: How I Run a Product
items: **Find the problem in the data:** where money or time is lost, read from production logs, the CRM and the receiving end.
**Decide and sequence:** bottleneck first; say no, in writing, to what the evidence does not support.
**Spec it with acceptance tests:** hard rules in code, judgment calls to the model, a human approval where a mistake is costly.
**Ship the smallest change** that tests the fix.
**Measure after launch and iterate:** harden what works; switch off what measures worse, even a technically impressive change.

steps.title: How I Automate
items: **Define the outcome** and the number that shows it happened.
**Map the workflow:** handoffs, repetitive work, failure points, the systems already in place.
**Choose the tool:** fixed rules for predictable steps, AI for research, classification and drafting, a human approval where a mistake would cost money, a customer or reputation.
**Build and integrate** with the existing systems; evaluate against real cases and reject changes that make it worse.
**Operate:** deploy, monitor from the receiving end, fix, document.

steps.title: How I Work
items: **Bring the recommendation, not just the research.** I investigate until I can say what matters, what I recommend and what happens next.
**Own the loose ends.** If information is falling between systems, finding the cause and closing the loop is part of the job.
**AI for leverage, not for judgment.** AI researches, drafts and executes; I stay accountable for priorities, verification and decisions.
**Build systems around recurring work.** A task that keeps eating attention becomes a documented workflow, a scheduled report or an agent-assisted process.
**Verify outcomes, not activity.** A “sent” status is not the result; I check that the business result actually happened.
